manifest.name: dsh-mcptoon
manifest.description: DSH plugin bundle that mounts mcptoon as an MCP server: compresses MCP tool discovery from 71,929 to 581 tokens across 255 tools (-99.2%, measured).

bundle.text:
# dsh-mcptoon bundle patch — mounts mcptoon into a DSH profile
#
# What this does: registers one MCP server entry through the official
# @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client bridge. The model then sees mcptoon's tools as
# `mcp__mcptoon__<tool>` — the same server-qualified shape other MCP hosts use.
#
# mcptoon is a gateway: `mcptoon serve` proxies your already-configured MCP
# servers behind one stdio connection and compresses their tool definitions
# with lossless TOON encoding, so the agent's tool-discovery step stops paying
# for full JSON schemas on every turn (71,929 -> 581 tokens across 255 tools,
# -99.2%, measured).
#
# Format note (from the DSH profile docs): a patch replaces whole entries, so
# every key of an entry it touches must be restated. This bundle only `insert`s,
# it never rewrites entries it does not own.
- insert:
    - id: mcp-mcptoon
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: mcptoon
        transport: stdio
        # `command` is a single executable name — never a shell string with
        # spaces baked in. Arguments live in `args` below, always as an array.
        command: mcptoon
        args: ['serve']

readme.text:
> English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) plugin bundle that mounts
[mcptoon](https://pypi.org/project/mcptoon/) as an MCP server in one command, so
the host agent discovers its MCP tools through mcptoon's compressed view instead
of paying full JSON schemas on every turn.

**Measured on a 255-tool workspace: tool discovery drops 71,929 -> 581 tokens across 255 tools (-99.2%, measured).** The encoding is lossless — `mcptoon` only
changes how tool definitions travel, never what they say.

After installing, the model sees `mcp__mcptoon__<tool>` — the same
server-qualified naming other MCP hosts use — and every upstream MCP server you
have already configured is proxied behind that single stdio connection.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:activeing123/dsh-mcptoon
```

Or, once the package is on npm:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mcptoon
```

Then restart the profile (or rely on HMR: editing the entry reconnects the bridge
without a process restart).

- Python 3.9+ with the mcptoon CLI on `PATH`: `pip install mcptoon` (zero
  dependencies, installs in seconds).
- Review the version before you upgrade: `pip install "mcptoon==<reviewed>"` is
  the safer default than an unconditional `--upgrade`.

readme.section: If the bridge does not come up
readme.text:
The bundle prints a self-check line at activation. When it says `not ready`, the
CLI is not where `command` points — common on Windows, where `pip` installs
`mcptoon.exe` next to an interpreter that is not on `PATH`, often under a path
containing a space (`C:\Program Files\...`).

Get the absolute path — the bundled doctor prints the exact override block:

readme.section: If the bridge does not come up
readme.text:
```sh
npx dsh-mcptoon-doctor          # or: node bin/doctor.mjs inside a checkout
python -c "import shutil;print(shutil.which('mcptoon'))"
```

Then override in your profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` — **one executable in
`command`, arguments in the `args` array, never a spaced shell string**:

```yaml
- id: mcp-mcptoon
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
  config:
    serverName: mcptoon

Sanity-check the composed profile without booting the app:

readme.section: If the bridge does not come up

readme.text:
This package is a *bundle*: its `package.json` declares
`dsh.bundle.patch`, and the patch file it points at inserts one entry into the
profile's plugin list — an instance of the official
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` bridge configured for `mcptoon serve`. The bundle
only ever `insert`s; it never rewrites entries it does not own.

readme.section: Relationship to the Claude Code plugin
readme.text:
mcptoon also ships a Claude Code plugin (`plugin.json` + `SKILL.md` +
`.mcp.json`) in the upstream repository. That packaging was the first to bundle
MCP management and compression as an installable plugin. **This DSH bundle is a
second host wrapper, not an endorsement or official support statement from
either project.**

Apache-2.0. mcptoon itself lives in [activeing123/mcptoon](https://github.com/activeing123/mcptoon)
and is distributed on PyPI.
